title: Glass and frame survey
audience: Trainees and workers on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision. The survey records observations for the supervisor; it is not a glazing or structural inspection.
learningOutcomes: Record the condition of glass, frames, seals and beading from ground level using a consistent survey sheet.
Separate visible defects from conditions that need a competent person to assess.
Apply stop-work and referral rules to glass or frames that look cracked, loose or unstable.

instruction.heading: Purpose of the survey
instruction.body: A glass and frame survey is a structured look at the windows or panels before cleaning starts. It records what can be seen from a safe position, so the supervisor can decide the method, the exclusion zone and whether the job should be stopped or referred. The survey is an observation record. It does not certify the glazing or the frame, and it does not replace a building or structural inspection. Keep that boundary clear in every record you write.

instruction.heading: What to look for
instruction.body: Survey each pane and frame in turn. Note cracks, chips and star breaks in the glass, and the position of each one. Look at the edges of the glass for chipping, and at the beading and gaskets for looseness, gaps or missing sections. Check the frame for corrosion, rot, cracking, movement and fixings that appear loose. Note any protective film, tinting, painted or frosted surfaces, and signs of previous repair or sealant. Record the glazing type where it is visible, such as toughened, laminated or insulated units, but do not state a type you cannot see.

instruction.heading: Separate defects from unknowns
instruction.body: A visible crack is a defect that you record and report. A panel that might be cracked behind a film, a frame that might be rotten inside its cavity, or a fixing you cannot reach is an unknown. Write unknowns in their own column. Do not turn an unknown into a finding of safe or unsafe. The supervisor or the building owner decides on the next step, and a competent person may be needed to assess the glazing or frame.

instruction.heading: Stop-work and referral triggers
instruction.body: Stop cleaning the affected panel, keep the zone clear, and refer the job when a pane is cracked through, a panel rattles or moves in its frame, a frame is loose from its fixings, glass is held only by sealant, or water or staining suggests a failure behind the glass. Do not push, lean on or test the glass to check it. Mark the area, report it in writing, and wait for a decision.

instruction.heading: Recording and communication
instruction.body: Use a survey sheet with a sketch or photograph for each elevation, numbered panels, and a column for each defect and unknown. Date the survey, name the surveyor and the supervisor, and record the weather at the time. Give the customer a written copy of the defects you found, and state clearly that the survey does not cover structural or glazing condition beyond what was visible from the ground.

instruction.heading: Boundary notes
instruction.body: This course does not teach glazing repair, sealant work, frame work or structural inspection of facades, and those tasks are out of scope. If a customer asks you to fix, seal or certify any of them, record the request and refer it. Completing this lesson does not grant any authority to inspect or certify a building, a facade or a glazing system. A ground-level survey avoids the height rules, but a ladder or platform does not: the national working-heights page says to work on the ground where possible (no date shown).

procedure: Set up at a safe ground-level position and confirm the exclusion zone before starting the survey.
Number each elevation and each pane or panel on the survey sheet or sketch.
Record visible cracks, chips, loose beading, missing gaskets, frame corrosion or movement, and any previous sealant or repair.
Mark items you cannot verify, such as hidden cavities or concealed fixings, as unknowns.
Apply the stop-work triggers and mark any affected panel as held.
Photograph each defect with the panel number visible, and note the time and weather.
Give the supervisor the survey, and record who has been told and what decision is pending.

workedExamples.situation: During a ground-level survey of a shopfront, a large pane shows a crack running from one corner. The lower beading is loose on one side, and the panel moves slightly when pressed by hand.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the surveyor do with this panel?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not press or test the panel further. Mark the panel as held, keep the public away from the area, and record the crack, the loose beading and the movement as defects. Photograph the panel with its number visible. Report it to the supervisor and the building owner in writing. Cleaning of that panel does not resume until a competent person has assessed it.

workedExamples.situation: A frame on a residential window looks sound from the ground, but a small area of paint is bubbling near the base and a fixing appears rusted.
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the bubbling paint and the rusted fixing as observed defects. The condition inside the frame cavity is an unknown and must be marked that way. Do not state that the frame is sound. Note the observations for the owner, and refer the frame to a competent person if the supervisor decides it affects safe access or cleaning.

equipmentAndPpe: Survey sheet or tablet form with numbered panels and defect and unknown columns
Camera or phone for photographs with the panel number visible
Measuring tape for panel dimensions where the job plan requires it
Eye protection and gloves as specified in the job pack

commonErrors.error: Recording a panel as safe because it looks intact from the ground.
commonErrors.prevention: Record only what was seen, and mark hidden condition as unknown.

commonErrors.error: Pressing or leaning on glass to test it.
commonErrors.prevention: Never test glass by hand. Mark it as held and refer it.

commonErrors.error: Offering to repair sealant or glazing during the survey.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the request and refer it, because repair work is out of scope.

commonErrors.error: Missing the date, the weather or the surveyor's name.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the header of the survey sheet before starting the survey.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Glass that is cracked, loose or held only by sealant can fall or shatter. Keep people clear, do not test the glass by hand, and refer the panel.
Facade structural inspection and glazing repair are out of scope for this course. This lesson grants no authority to inspect or certify a building or glazing system.

Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to work at height, inspect a facade, or certify glazing. Where a boom-type platform is used, a WP licence applies at a boom length of 11 metres or more in New South Wales, and a shorter boom may not need it there. In Queensland, platforms under 11 metres are not included in the WP licence definition. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there.

qualityStandard: Every pane and frame in the scope is numbered and recorded, or marked as not surveyed with a reason.
Defects and unknowns are recorded in separate columns.
Held panels are marked and the supervisor is told before any cleaning resumes.
The survey states its limits in writing.
documentationEvidence: Survey sheet with date, surveyor, supervisor, weather and numbered panels
Defect list with photographs showing the panel number
Unknowns list with the reason each item could not be verified
Hold or referral record with the person notified
summary: A survey records what is visible from a safe position and does not certify the glazing or frame.
Keep visible defects and unknowns separate.
Stop, hold and refer any cracked, loose or unstable panel.
Glazing repair, sealant work and structural inspection are out of scope.

knowledgeChecks.question: A pane has a visible crack and loose beading. How should it be recorded?
options: As safe, because it is at ground level and easy to reach
As a defect, with the panel marked as held and reported
As a sealant job to be quoted later on by the office
As unknown and then cleaned anyway on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct way to check a pane that may be cracked behind a film?
options: Press on it firmly with the flat of the palm of the hand to test it
Tap it to listen for a crack in the glass, the frame and the film
Record it as an unknown and refer it, without pressing or testing it
Assume it is fine if the film is intact and clean on the outside

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks for a loose frame to be re-sealed during the survey. What must the surveyor do?
options: Re-seal it, because it is quick and easy to do on the spot today
Quote a price on the spot for the sealant work and the frame
Ignore the request and carry on with the survey and the report
Record the request and refer it, because sealant work is out of scope

knowledgeChecks.question: Which entry is correct for a frame cavity that cannot be seen?
options: Unknown until a competent person has assessed it
Sound, with no defects found at all in the cavity
Compliant with the standard for the frame and sill
Rotten at the base of the frame and the sill

knowledgeChecks.question: Does this survey certify the glazing or the frame?
options: Yes, once signed by the surveyor and dated by the client today
No, it records what was visible and does not certify condition
Yes, if the customer agrees to the survey in writing today
Only for toughened glass in the frame of the house
